replacements.text: Strongest feature: Craig distinguishes necessity from chance, invokes physics against required conditions, and presents life-permitting contingency as favoring design while rejoining Flew’s objection. Principal limitation: Contingency rebuts necessity without establishing design, since “incomprehensible” improbability supplies neither a probability distribution nor assessment of observer selection, undiscovered mechanisms, and designer predictions. Live burden: Craig must provide likelihoods demonstrating design predicts life-permitting conditions better than chance, selection, or unknown law; Flew must identify what evidence could warrant design without universes or designer-production knowledge. Locked score: The exact 70 reflects logical coherence 69 for incomplete elimination, evidence warrant 62 for unspecified probabilities, responsiveness 75 for partial contact, relevance and burden 82 for centrality, precision and clarity 75 for intelligible yet unauditable alternatives, and calibration and charity 58 for overstatement.

Strongest feature: Craig answers Flew’s challenge by proposing specified improbability as design evidence and using implements to show unlikelihood supporting inference beyond complexity. Principal limitation: The analogy neither defines specification nor supplies probability distribution or designer likelihood, while arrowhead identification depends upon knowledge of agents and production processes unavailable for universe selection. Live burden: Craig must demonstrate life-permitting conditions meet a noncircular specification and discriminate design from selection or undiscovered law; Flew must engage the criterion rather than reiterating artifact recognition. Locked score: The exact 74 reflects logical coherence 72 for incomplete transfer, evidence warrant 64 for the background-knowledge disanalogy, responsiveness 86 for direct contact, relevance and burden 78 for centrality, precision and clarity 76 for undefined specification, and calibration and charity 67 for understatement.
